citations.quote: This chapter focuses on a relatively simple, transparent model that is an excellent starting point for studying these issues, the Solow growth model.
Equation (1.19) is the key equation of the Solow model. It states that the rate of change of the capital stock per unit of effective labor is the difference between two terms.
Aggregate demand tells us only the relationship between the price level and the amount of output demanded at those prices.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: The Solow model embeds CRS production f(k) with exogenous saving s, depreciation delta, and labor/technology growth (n,g); per-effective-worker capital k-tilde evolves k-tilde-dot = s*f(k-tilde) - (n+g+delta)*k-tilde and converges to k* where saving equals break-even investment; long-run per-capita output growth is the exogenous technology rate g.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Solow Growth Model
